elements.element: Services must be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: Section 19.1 expressly provides that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.

elements.element: Deliverables and software must materially conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: Sections 19.1 and 19.2 require Deliverables and software to materially conform to their documentation.

elements.element: The software conformance warranty must last 12 months after delivery.
elements.evidence: Section 19.2 provides only 90 days after delivery and expressly disclaims correction or refund obligations thereafter.

elements.element: The Services conformance warranty must last 90 days.
elements.evidence: Section 19.1 contains a Services conformance warranty, but no express 90-day post-performance or post-delivery warranty period. Section 19.2's 90-day period applies only to Deliverables and software.

elements.element: Repair must be available as a remedy for breach of the applicable warranties.
elements.evidence: Section 19.4 requires Vendor to promptly repair a nonconforming item at no charge.

elements.element: Replacement must be available as a remedy for breach of the applicable warranties.
elements.evidence: Section 19.4 requires Vendor to promptly replace a nonconforming item at no charge.

elements.element: A refund must be available as a remedy if repair, replacement, or re-performance cannot be completed within a reasonable period.
elements.evidence: Section 19.4 allows Customer to terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid if Vendor cannot cure within a reasonable period.

elements.element: Vendor must warrant compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no compliance-with-laws warranty.

elements.element: Vendor must warrant that the Services, Deliverables, and software contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no malicious-code warranty.

elements.element: Software must materially conform to its documentation.
elements.evidence: Section 19.2 expressly requires software delivered to Customer to materially conform to its documentation.

elements.element: The software conformance warranty must last 90 days after delivery.
elements.evidence: Section 19.2 expressly provides a 90-day period after delivery for software conformance.

elements.element: Services must materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications.
elements.evidence: Section 19.1 expressly warrants that Services will materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications.

elements.element: The Services conformance warranty must last 30 days.
elements.evidence: No express 30-day Services warranty period is stated. The 90-day period in Section 19.2 applies to Deliverables and software, which are separately identified from Services in Section 19.1.

elements.element: Repair must be available as a remedy for breach of the applicable warranties.
elements.evidence: Section 19.4 requires prompt repair at no charge.

elements.element: Replacement must be available as a remedy for breach of the applicable warranties.
elements.evidence: Section 19.4 requires prompt replacement at no charge.

elements.element: A refund must be available if repair, replacement, or re-performance cannot be completed within a reasonable period.
elements.evidence: Section 19.4 permits termination of the affected item and a refund of Fees paid if Vendor cannot cure within a reasonable period.

result.reason: The redline establishes the fallback 90-day software warranty and retains the required remedies, but it does not expressly establish the fallback 30-day Services warranty. The unqualified Services warranty in Section 19.1 does not state the required post-performance duration, and the defined drafting distinguishes Services from Deliverables and software. The preferred position also fails because software is covered for only 90 days rather than 12 months, the Services warranty lacks an express 90-day duration, and warranties concerning legal compliance and malicious code are absent. The margin comment is non-operative and cannot cure these omissions.
